header.running_head: An Exchange of Words between Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Amr bin Sa'eed (RA) and Hadhrat Khaalid bin Sa'eed (RA) Advises his Brother to Assist Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)

blocks.text: Sa'eed (RA) rejoined, "If we fight, it will not be for you because we fight only for Allaah." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then said, "May Allaah guide you! You have spoken well." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then said to Hadhrat Amr bin Sa'eed (RA), "Please be seated. May Allaah shower His mercy on you. In saying what you heard him say, Umar did not intend to hurt or to insult any Muslim. All he intended by what he said was to encourage those who were hesitant to fight in Jihaad." Thereafter, Hadhrat Khaalid bin Sa'eed (RA) (the brother of Hadhrat Amr bin Sa'eed (RA)) stood up and said, "The Khalifah of Rasulullaah ﷺ is right. Do be seated, dear brother." When Hadhrat Amr bin Sa'eed (RA) sat down, Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) continued, "All praises belong to Allaah besides Whom none is worthy of worship. Who has sent Muhammad ﷺ with guidance and the true Deen to make it dominate over all other religions even though the Mushrikeen abhor it. All praises are due to Allaah Who fulfils His promises, Who makes them come to realisation and Who destroys His enemies. We neither oppose you nor have any opposition amongst ourselves. You are a well-wishing and concerned leader and we are prepared to march whenever you command and prepared to obey you whenever you issue an order." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was extremely pleased by this speech and said, "May Allaah reward you well, my brother and friend! You had accepted Islaam willingly, migrated with the hope of reward when you escaped from the Kuffaar with your Deen so that Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ may be pleased and so that the Kalimah may be elevated. You are one of the commanders of the people, so prepare to march. May Allaah shower His mercy on you." Thereafter, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) descended from the pulpit. Hadhrat Khaalid bin Sa'eed (RA) then left to make the necessary preparations. In the meanwhile, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) instructed Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) to make the following announcement: "O people! March in Jihaad against the Romans in Shaam!" There were no doubts amongst the people that Hadhrat Khaalid bin Sa'eed (RA) was their commander. He was the first to reach the army camp, after which people started arriving there in tens, twenties, thirties, forties, fifties and hundreds. Eventually, a very large army had gathered. Accompanied by several leading Sahabah (RA), Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) proceeded to the camp one day. Although he saw an impressive number of men, he did not think that the number was adequate to fight the Romans. Turning to his companions, he asked, "What would you say if I send this number of men to Shaam?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "I do not think that this number is sufficient for the large Roman army." Turning to the others, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) asked, "What do you men think?" they replied, "We second the opinion of Umar." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then said, "Should I then rather not write to the people of Yemen, calling them to Jihaad and encouraging them with the rewards for Jihaad?" All his companions shared his opinion and said, "That is an excellent idea! Go ahead." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then wrote the letter.
